cautions: FORMULAS AT LITERACY LEVEL: teach the TIME VALUE OF MONEY formulas with simple original arithmetic — FV = PV × (1 + r)^n with small numbers (e.g. $100 at 5% for 2 years = $110.25); NPV as 'present value of inflows minus outflows' with a 2-year example; IRR as 'the discount rate where NPV = 0' with intuition only (no trial-and-error math). NO bond-pricing formula depth, NO CAPM formula, NO option pricing.
NO INVESTMENT ADVICE: never recommend specific investments; teaching 'diversification reduces risk' is educational, 'buy index funds' is advice — keep the line.

SIBLING SUBJECTS: accounting owns statement preparation and the four ratio formulas; finance re-uses them as decision tools (reference the accounting lessons). personal-finance owns household budgeting/saving depth. introduction-to-business finance-basics owns the overview.

risk/return: teach the general positive relationship (higher expected return carries higher risk) with original examples; risk-free rate as a concept (Treasury bills), not a live number unless time-anchored.
financial-markets: primary vs secondary markets, exchanges vs OTC — factual, no hype; inflation: general definition + why lenders care (real vs nominal, stated simply, no forecasting).

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D (≥1 C, ≥1 D per topic; max 3 of 5 per slot). Verify keys from the file yourself. BANNED: 'Which statement best defines X used in this lesson?' stems — write topic-specific questions (e.g. 'What does the time value of money mean?', 'Which discount rate makes NPV equal zero?').
